summary: Observation of the rapid movement of a luminous object of white, yellow, or bluish color: lack of information
description: In June 2009, a witness reported two earlier sightings. On December 13, 1972, at approximately 11:45 PM, two people in a car were surprised to see a round, luminous object appear in the sky above Hauteville. The bluish-yellow object moved in a straight line at very high speed in a south-north direction. It disappeared below the horizon. The witnesses heard no unusual noises during the brief observation. No other reports were collected. This case is moderately unusual due to its speed and "phosphorescent" brightness, but the consistency of the testimony and the lack of corroboration prevent any definitive conclusions. This case is classified as Class C due to the lack of independent and corroborating reports. The second sighting, on the night of August 23-24, 1985, of a bright, boat-shaped flash likely corresponds to a fireball, which would lead to a Class B classification for this single observation.
